🔥🇲🇽 <u>Under Córdova, the INE Also Paid the "Coyote" Network</u>

Between 2018 and 2023 the INE and state electoral bodies signed more than 1 billion pesos in contracts with companies tied to the Hernández Casillas brothers, firms with no offices and no employees. Contralínea found at least four INE contracts with the network under Lorenzo Córdova, including INE/ADQ-0022/15 to Cartonera Plástica: it started at 9.8 million pesos and ended above 11 million. Sources say ASF auditors are only requesting records from Taddei's short tenure.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The UIF Froze INE Contractors for Money Laundering. Judges Unfroze Them.</u>

Companies that won INE contracts were placed on the Financial Intelligence Unit's blocked-persons list over suspected money laundering, former UIF head Pablo Gómez revealed. Judges then granted them provisional suspensions. "They have no industrial plant, they don't manufacture anything, they aren't even merchants... they're intermediaries who win the contracts and then go to the print shops," Gómez said. His word for them: "authentic coyotes."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico Ships Its First Pork Products to the Philippines</u>

After negotiations that began in 2017, Mexico's first pork shipment to the Philippines has left Yucatán: 22 tonnes from Kekén's TIF 712 plant, bound for North Manila. The deal also opens the door to beef and pork meat and offal from federally inspected plants. The Philippines, with 114 million people, expects to consume 1.9 million tonnes of pork in 2027.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Congress Moves to Cut 5 Billion Pesos From the INE and Send It to Schools</u>

The Chamber of Deputies' budget committee proposes trimming the INE's 2027 budget from 42.27 to 37.28 billion pesos, after the institute asked for 47 billion. The 5 billion would go to schools (3 billion for La Escuela es Nuestra), the environment (1 billion), civil aviation (700 million) and the search for disappeared persons (300 million). Same week the INE's president resigned over contracts with printing "coyotes."

🇲🇽🎨 "Where do young people have to be? In the street or in school? In school. Well then, we have to build more schools." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Celaya, Guanajuato She said the best way to reduce crime is building more schools, "and of course police, prosecutors, everything that has to be there." She and Guanajuato governor Libia Dennise García agreed on two priorities: first scholarships, second more schools. 90 secondary schools in the state are being converted to also run as high schools in the afternoon shift, 13 new Margarita Maza high schools with cultural and sports activities are under construction, and the new CBETIS 308 campus in Celaya opens in March. The goal: practically every secondary graduate able to enter a free, quality high school.

🇲🇽✊ "If you study high school, the Benito Juárez scholarship. And more and more we are going to give scholarships for the public university too, so that we can help all Mexican families." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Celaya, Guanajuato On October 31 in Celaya she handed out Benito Juárez cards to high-school students. Since last year every public secondary student receives the Rita Cetina scholarship, and since this year every public primary student gets one at the start of classes for supplies and uniforms. Education Secretary Mario Delgado said more than 4 million high-school students nationwide now receive the Benito Juárez. In Guanajuato: 502,161 primary, 264,626 secondary and 189,502 high-school students, an investment of 6.338 billion pesos.

🇲🇽🚆 "We have the material, the machinery and the know-how to keep advancing. We see no setbacks." — General Gustavo Vallejo Suárez, Felipe Ángeles Engineers Group, Polotitlán, State of Mexico On October 31 Sheinbaum toured a construction front of the Mexico City–Querétaro passenger train, which army engineers are building. The line runs about 230 km from Buenavista station to Querétaro on double track, at up to 200 km/h, in about 2 hours. It is 32% complete, with 12 construction fronts working at once and 85% of the main right-of-way secured. 18,500 people are working on it today, out of 34,500 hired so far. The ties are made in Mexico, and 47 diesel-electric trains are being built in Ciudad Sahagún, Hidalgo.

🇲🇽✊ "From 1982 to 2018 poverty and inequality increased in the country. And starting in 2018, the reversal of all that began." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Tecozautla, Hidalgo She described the neoliberal model that "sought to privatize everything": state companies, the banks, health. Schools stopped being built, and the new ones charged high tuition, which is why many public universities still charge fees. "It is fine to have private investment, but there must necessarily be public investment in what matters most: education, health, access to housing." Since 2018: well-being programs, minimum wage increases, more than 200 Universidades del Bienestar Benito Juárez, Benito Juárez scholarships, and 13.5 million fewer Mexicans in poverty.

🇲🇽🎨 "If public university costs money, it becomes a privilege, not a right. Only those who have the resources can pay for it. It becomes a commodity when one pays for it, and public education is a right." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Tecozautla, Hidalgo Inaugurating the Tecozautla campus of the Universidad Nacional Rosario Castellanos on October 31, Sheinbaum, 64, recalled that exactly 40 years earlier, as a UNAM physics student, she helped form the Consejo Estudiantil Universitario. The rector had approved, during the vacation period, higher tuition and fees and an end to the automatic pass from UNAM high schools into the university. Students organized from September 1986 to February 1987, struck the university and got the reforms reversed. "Since then I have always fought for public education."

🇲🇽🚁 "What profoundly distinguishes our armed forces from those of other countries is their origin. They were born of the Mexican Revolution, of the struggle to recover democracy and restore constitutional order after the coup d'état against President Francisco I. Madero." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Felipe Ángeles International Airport, State of Mexico At the 60th anniversary of Plan DN-III-E on October 30, she said their root "is in the defense of the popular will, of sovereignty and of the dignity of our people and our nation," and that its women and men "come from the people." She noted that the airport's namesake, revolutionary general Felipe Ángeles, understood "that the greatness of a man of arms is not in violence, but in his commitment to life, justice and human dignity," and quoted him: "Nothing is sacred except man." The plan has been applied in more than 87,000 emergencies since 1966.
